name: model-viewer
title: Model Viewer
description: A 3D model (glTF or GLB) in a stage that turns with drag, wheel, pinch and keys, with views, zoom, reset, animation clips, morph weights (a Float32Array aligned with the target names, or by name) and ARKit expressions eased in the render loop, and an optional floor (a grid, a contact shadow) in the theme's colours. A new model fades in over the old one, keeping its weights. controls="gestures" keeps drag and keys without the bar, for controls of your own through handleRef and useModelViewerControls. The three.js scene (react-three-fiber) is a separate chunk, loaded when the stage nears the viewport and only with WebGL; a poster stands in until then and without WebGL. Agents get rotate, zoom, reset, setView, play, pause and selectClip.

files.content:
import type { ModelViewerView } from "@/components/ui/model-viewer-math"

type ModelViewerLabels = {
  controls: string
  views: string
  view: Record<ModelViewerView, string>
  zoomIn: string
  zoomOut: string
  reset: string
  play: string
  clip: string
  /** Read after the stage's name while it has focus. */
  keyboard: string
  unsupported: string
  error: string
}

const modelViewerLabels: ModelViewerLabels = {
  controls: "3D view controls",
  views: "View",
  view: { front: "Front", "three-quarter": "¾", side: "Side", back: "Back" },
  zoomIn: "Zoom in",
  zoomOut: "Zoom out",
  reset: "Reset view",
  play: "Play animation",
  clip: "Animation",
  keyboard: "Drag or use the arrow keys to turn, + and - to zoom, Home to reset.",
  unsupported: "3D isn't available in this browser.",
  error: "The 3D model could not be loaded.",
}

export { modelViewerLabels }
export type { ModelViewerLabels }

docs: `<ModelViewer model alt poster summary aspectRatio view defaultView onViewChange framing clip defaultClip onClipChange playing defaultPlaying onPlayingChange loop speed weights targetNames expressions material background floor autoRotate controls handleRef load overlay sceneChildren onLoad onError error labels>`: `model` is a URL, its bytes (an ArrayBuffer) or a loaded scene (`{ scene, animations }`). The stage is `role="img"` named by `alt`, described by the keyboard hint and the visible `summary`; while it has focus, arrows turn the model, + and - zoom and Home resets. Views are `front`, `three-quarter`, `side` and `back`; free rotation sets the view to `null`. `framing` is `"full"` or a sphere of the model (`{ center: [x, y, z], radius }` in its own units), like a face for a close-up. `weights` are morph weights: a Float32Array (or numbers) aligned with `targetNames`, which default to the GLB's `extras.targetNames` (meshes in scene order), or a map by name; values aren't clamped, so a principal component can be negative. `expressions` maps ARKit names (`mouthSmileLeft`) to weights on the `expr.<name>` targets, over `weights`. They ease inside the render loop with no allocation and no React render per frame; a target never set is left to clips. A new `model` loads under the shown one and takes over its camera, weights and clip time: it replaces it at once when the two look the same (meshes, vertex counts, targets, colours), or fades in over it. `playing` left out (or `null`) plays the clip once loaded, except under reduced motion, which also drops auto-rotation and turns every camera move and swap into a jump. `material="toon"` swaps in a three-tone toon material. `floor` draws a grid disc and a contact shadow under the model's feet in the theme's muted foreground, and pools the card colour over the stage. `controls` is `true` (the bar under the stage, and drag, wheel, pinch and keys), `"gestures"` (the gestures and keys without the bar) or `false` (a still stage); with `"gestures"`, `handleRef` hands over the viewer's handle and `useModelViewerControls(handle)` its status, view, clips and playing, rendering only when one changes, for a toolbar of your own that calls `handle.api`. Theme colours in the canvas are read again when the theme changes. The canvas draws on demand (`frameloop="demand"`), only while the camera, a clip, a weight or a swap moves, and not at all while the stage is out of view or the tab is hidden. Without WebGL, or when loading fails (`labels.error`, announced at once), the poster stays with a message. `preloadModelViewer()` starts loading the scene chunk early; `sceneChildren` puts three.js content of your own inside the canvas, where `ModelViewerSceneContext` gives the viewer's handle and the model's rig. Agent calls before the model has loaded, or for a clip it doesn't have, throw with the reason.
